speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to understand the pattern of your symptoms, does the weakness in your arms and legs affect the same side of your body or different sides?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest, along with diplopia specifically triggered by upgaze and downgaze, is highly characteristic of this condition.
